audience: Working adults and general learners. General-purpose language learning: every lesson is built around a real-life goal; Cambridge objectives no longer decide what goes into a lesson.

naming.note: A level is made of lessons (the old course called them units); a lesson is made of sections; a section is made of steps.

schedule.note: Starter to Level 3 is 196 study days (9 months, about 392 hours); Level 4 is 42 more (about 84 hours). Weeks are full: each week of holidays moves the end date by a week.

levels.name: Letters & Sounds
levels.summary: A reading and writing strand for adults who cannot yet read English letters. It runs alongside Starter rather than before it, so learners also start speaking English in their first week.
levels.for: Adults who cannot yet read English letters. A five-minute check at the start sends them here; everyone else skips it.
levels.exit: Can read and write short regular words sound by sound, read the commonest irregular words, and read a simple sentence aloud.
levels.ends: Reading check: 10 regular words, 5 common irregular words and one sentence, read aloud.

bridge.title: Bridge A · English letters, different sounds
bridge.text: For learners who already read another language written in Latin letters, such as Somali: letter names versus sounds, the five short vowels, and th, sh and ch.

bridge.title: Bridge B · One sound, many spellings
bridge.text: ai, a_e and ay; ee and ea; ie, i_e and igh; oa, o_e and ow.

levels.name: Starter — First Steps
levels.summary: Everyday English for adults with little or no English. Speaking and listening come first; every line has audio and every word a picture where possible.
levels.for: Adults with little or no English. Learners who cannot yet read English letters take Letters & Sounds alongside it.
levels.exit: Can greet people and give personal details, count and deal with prices, name everyday things, people, places, food, clothes and work, say what they need and where it hurts, and ask the way, in short phrases.
levels.ends: A review day and the Starter check, reported for each skill separately. It is not a barrier to Level 1.
levels.reader: an illustrated Pre-A1 story of 100–200 words

levels.name: Level 1 — Everyday English
levels.summary: English for daily life: personal details, home, shopping, routines, food, health, clothes, getting around and simple plans.
levels.for: Learners who finished Starter, or whose placement test shows A1.
levels.exit: Can read and understand short familiar texts, ask and answer simple questions about people, places, routines and events, follow and give simple instructions, and write short notes and messages joined with and, but and because.
levels.ends: A review day, then the A1 check (one day) in the four skills, reported for each skill separately.
